summary: Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1985–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University. He served on Leiden University's faculty as a lecturer (1967) and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.

Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history, Ditte Bandini-König was a visiting fellow at the Collège de France (1992–1993) and a collaborator at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Specializing in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, Diwakar Acharya studied under Ramananda Giri and Albrecht Wezler at the University of Hamburg (PhD). He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, Kyoto University (2006–2016), and the University of Oxford (from 2016).
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu. He served as abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at St. Petersburg University (~1886–1890) and served at the University of Tartu from approximately 1898 to 1920.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Menpa Bum Rampa Tendzin Döndrub, and Kunzang Pelden, and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and numerous other disciples.

Dominic Goodall works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan and completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He became a professor at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2000.

Dominic Sur specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Virginia under David F. Germano, Khenpo Lama Chönam, Karen Christina Lang, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer. He held a post at Utah State University.

Dominik Haas works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Marion Rastelli, was a DOC Fellow at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and was affiliated with the University of Vienna in 2022.

Dominik Wujastyk specializes in Indology and history, having studied at the University of London and University of Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1982–2002), University College London (2002–2009), University of Vienna (2009–2015), and University of Alberta (2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1978–1984). He joined the faculty of the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1987.

Dominique-Sila Khan worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1988–1993) and served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He was a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and later served on the faculty at Texas Christian University (attested 2001).

Don Handelman worked in anthropology and religious studies, completing studies at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester. He served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from approximately 1972 to 2008.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist and historian who studied at Richmond College, Galle, and under Wilhelm Geiger at Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. He served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1928) and taught at the University of London (~1918–1930).

Donald A. Ringe is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Kentucky, University of Oxford, and Yale University under Warren Cowgill. He taught Classics at Bard College (1983–1985) and joined the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1985.

Donald Capps worked in religious studies and pastoral theology, studying at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary from 1981 to 2009.

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda, and served on the faculty at the University of Massachusetts Amherst from around 1976 to 2012.
